title: Could Daydreaming at Work Unlock Your Best Problem-Solving Skills?
titleZh: 发呆这件小事，也许比你想的更有用
summary:
无论是在学校还是在职场，走神通常被视为一种不受欢迎的行为。学生常被要求“别发呆了”，员工也会被提醒将注意力放回眼前的工作。然而，最新的研究表明，在适当的引导和支持下，那些看似分心的瞬间，其实可能是解决复杂问题的一种有效途径。由美国和荷兰的研究人员组成的一个联合团队发现，那些充满好奇心、并允许自己在面对工作挑战时自由思考的人，更容易迎来豁然开朗的顿悟时刻。这种灵感的火花不仅能激发创新的解决方案，还能帮助人重新感受到工作的意义。

来源：Discover；作者：Jenny Lehmann；原文发布时间：2025-10-08 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: At school or in the office, mind wandering is often frowned upon. Students are told to “snap out of it,” and employees are nudged back to focus on the task at hand. Yet new research suggests that with the right support, what looks like distraction might in fact be a powerful tool for solving tough problems. A joint team of researchers from the U.S. and the Netherlands has found that curious individuals who allow themselves to daydream around work challenges are more likely to experience strong epiphanies. These flashes of insight cannot only spark innovative solutions but also renew a sense of meaning in their careers.
paragraphs.contentZh: 无论是在学校还是在职场，走神通常被视为一种不受欢迎的行为。学生常被要求“别发呆了”，员工也会被提醒将注意力放回眼前的工作。然而，最新的研究表明，在适当的引导和支持下，那些看似分心的瞬间，其实可能是解决复杂问题的一种有效途径。由美国和荷兰的研究人员组成的一个联合团队发现，那些充满好奇心、并允许自己在面对工作挑战时自由思考的人，更容易迎来豁然开朗的顿悟时刻。这种灵感的火花不仅能激发创新的解决方案，还能帮助人重新感受到工作的意义。

paragraphs.contentEn: “For years, I was fascinated by the phenomenon of epiphanies, but I wasn’t sure how to study them, and I found the challenges that go with pursuing a new and uncharted line of research a bit daunting,” said Erik Dane, professor of organizational behavior at Olin Business School at Washington University, in a press release. The team’s findings, published in the Journal of Management, may even encourage workplaces to consider workshops that embrace mind wandering as a path to those light-bulb moments.
paragraphs.contentZh: 华盛顿大学奥林商学院组织行为学教授埃里克·戴恩在一份新闻稿中表示：“多年来，我一直对顿悟这一现象很感兴趣，但始终不确定该从何入手进行研究。而且探索一条全新且尚未被涉足的研究路径，也让我感到相当艰难。”该团队的研究成果已发表在《管理学》期刊上，这些发现甚至可能促使企业考虑开设相关工作坊，将自由思考纳入培训，作为引发灵光乍现的一种有效方式。

paragraphs.contentEn: The research involved business administration students, alumni, and aspiring business leaders in three different studies. Participants were assessed for their ability to have work-related epiphanies and were guided through professional workshops and individual coaching sessions designed to strengthen leadership skills. Exercises encouraged students to reflect on key life events, the legacies they hoped to leave, and even their own mortality. Crucially, participants were also given time to let their minds wander. Daydreaming wasn’t treated as a lapse in focus but as an intentional part of the process.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这项研究由三项独立实验组成，参与者包含工商管理专业的学生、毕业生以及有志成为企业领袖的人士。研究评估了参与者在工作中获得顿悟的能力，并通过专业工作坊和一对一辅导来提升其领导力。在训练过程中，研究人员引导参与者回顾人生中的重要经历，思考自己希望留下的影响，甚至直面死亡这一议题。其中最关键的一环，是为参与者预留了自由遐想的时间。在研究中，放飞思绪并不被视为是注意力不集中的表现，而是整个流程中有意设计的组成部分。

paragraphs.contentEn: The results were clear: Participants who allowed themselves to daydream while working through a challenge were more likely to experience meaningful insights. And those naturally drawn to tackling complex problems, typically more curious and motivated to expand their knowledge, gained the most. For them, daydreaming was less about escape and more about finding new pathways forward.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究结果清晰地表明：在面对复杂问题时，允许自己思绪适当游离的参与者，更容易获得有价值的洞见。特别是那些生性乐于挑战复杂难题的人（通常充满好奇心且渴望拓展知识），从中收获最大。对他们而言，自由遐想并不是逃避现实，而是一种探索新思路的有效方式。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Mind wandering is a particularly useful way to solve problems because it redirects attention away from existing solutions and helps people engage in imaginative thinking, entertaining brand new possibilities,” said Markus Baer, professor of organizational behavior at Washington University, in the news release. He added that daydreaming provides a more playful and liberating approach compared to conventional, formal problem-solving methods.
paragraphs.contentZh: 华盛顿大学组织行为学教授马库斯·贝尔在新闻稿中表示：“思绪游离是一种尤为有效的解决问题方式，因为它能让人将注意力从既有方案上转移，投入更具想象力的思考，从而开启全新的可能。”他补充说，相较于传统而正式的问题解决方法，白日梦式的思维更加轻松自由，也更富创造性。

paragraphs.contentEn: Dane agreed: “When you daydream, you’re more likely to let go of assumptions — including unhelpful or outdated beliefs about yourself — and to think in flexible and innovative ways. And this opens the door to experiencing strong epiphanies.” Sometimes, Dane explained, stepping back to see the bigger picture with a bit of free imagination can deliver not only fresh solutions but also a stronger sense of purpose.
paragraphs.contentZh: 戴恩对此表示认同：“当人们任由思绪漫游时，更容易放下固有的思维假设——包括那些无益或早已过时的自我认知——从而以更灵活、更具创新性的方式思考。这也为强烈的顿悟时刻创造了条件。”戴恩进一步解释说，有时候退一步，用一点自由的想象来审视全局，不仅能催生新的解决方案，也能让人重新体会到工作的意义。

paragraphs.contentEn: The researchers argue that organizations and business schools should recognize the value of problem-solving daydreaming by offering workshops and programs to nurture the skill. Since many people are searching for greater career guidance, this research suggests they may benefit from first looking inward. Instead of waiting for external circumstances to inspire them, intentional reflection and daydreaming could help create the breakthroughs they seek.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究人员主张，企业组织和商学院应当意识到“以解决问题为导向的走神”的价值，并通过工作坊或培训项目来帮助人们培养这种能力。当下，许多人都在寻求更明确职业方向，这项研究表明，我们或许可以从内在反思开始。与其等待外部机遇带来灵感，有意识的自我反思与思绪游离，或许更有助于实现我们所寻求的突破。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Epiphanies are one of the most memorable and impactful psychological events that people experience in their lives — and my research has helped me understand when and why people experience epiphanies and how epiphanies shape the ways in which people navigate their careers, gain self-confidence, collaborate with colleagues, and serve as leaders in organizations,” said Dane.
paragraphs.contentZh: 戴恩表示：“顿悟是人生中最难忘、也最具影响力的心理体验之一——我的研究帮助我理解了人们产生顿悟的时机与缘由，并揭示了这种体验如何塑造人们的职业生涯规划、自信心建立、团队协作乃至组织领导力的展现。”
